_note: Which checks ops/ci.sh runs where, and WHY each exception exists. Read by the gates class. Every entry needs a reason, and ci.sh PRINTS every exception on every run — a check that stops running must never do so quietly. That is the failure shape of the runaway launchd job found 2026-08-13: a clean report that was clean because nothing was looking.
_quarantine_history: vault-drift-watch-selftest.py was quarantined 2026-08-13 as FLAKY ('4 of 5 runs pass and the failing case DIFFERS between runs'), diagnosed as probable same-second mtime resolution. That diagnosis was wrong and the entry is removed. The real cause was a hardcoded, process-shared scratch path: every run rmtree'd the same fixture tree, so concurrent runs deleted each other's fixtures mid-test and the losing case varied with the interleaving. Fixed by giving each process its own mkdtemp base. Evidence: 3 concurrent runs failed every time before, 5 concurrent runs pass 24/24 after, and a single run passed 6 for 6 both before and after — which is why a sequential re-run could not reproduce it and mtime looked plausible.

local_only.reason: Exercises LaunchAgent load and idempotent retry. launchd is macOS. Evidence: 'LaunchAgent load failure and idempotent retry both stay nonzero' failed on the ubuntu runner 2026-08-13, run 31750582043.

_evidence_note: Each local_only entry names an observed platform limit or an explicit production-access policy. Portable failures are fixed rather than excluded: test-review-council.py needed zsh installed and its own out/ dirs created, and test-record-home-gate.py had a hardcoded $HOME path. Excluding a check is the last resort, not the first.
